LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source URL from the official Todoist domain (electron-dl.todoist.net) and pins a sha256 checksum for the AppImage. No top-level code executes any dangerous operations (no eval, no curl|bash, no obfuscation). The functions `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` are not run during the `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` step. `pkgver()` is not defined, so nothing executes there. Downloading and extracting the source (with `noextract` preventing extraction) is the only operation, which is standard and expected. No genuine malicious behavior is present.
</details>
<summary>No risk; PKGBUILD performs standard source fetch with pinned checksum.</summary>
</security_assessment>

audits.body:
Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/todoist-appimage.git...
Cloned todoist-appimage
Analyzing todoist-appimage AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from the official Todoist domain (`electron-dl.todoist.net`) over HTTPS, which is expected and safe for this package type. The `sha256sums_x86_64` array contains a valid checksum, indicating intent to verify the AppImage, so there is no reliance on `SKIP`. The top-level scope of the PKGBUILD contains no command substitutions or immediate execution of dangerous code. The `pkgver()` function is not defined, so no dynamic version fetching occurs. Sourcing the PKGBUILD during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` or `--nobuild` will not execute any malicious payloads. While the `prepare()` and `build()` functions modify the desktop file and extract the AppImage, these stages are not reached under `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`, so they are out of scope for this narrow gate. No data exfiltration or remote code execution occurs during source fetch and parse.
</details>
<summary>
No malicious code execution during source fetch and parse
</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- No malicious code execution during source fetch and parse

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD retrieves a prebuilt AppImage from Todoist's official download server (`electron-dl.todoist.net`) and extracts it to install the application in a standard, reproducible way. The source URL is legitimate and specific to the declared version, and the checksum for the x86_64 binary is provided and matches the expected format. No code is compiled or downloaded from untrusted sources during the build process.

The prepare() and build() functions perform typical modifications to the extracted `.desktop` file—adjusting the `Exec` line to disable sandboxing and ensure proper desktop integration—and include defensive checks to prevent malformed entries. These changes are transparent, well-documented in comments, and consistent with packaging best practices for AppImages on Arch Linux. Permissions are also corrected post-extraction to ensure accessibility.

All operations are confined to the package build environment, and no network requests, obfuscated commands, or dangerous scripts (e.g., curl|bash, eval, base64 decoding) are present. The use of `chmod`, `sed`, `grep`, and `install` is appropriate and non-malicious. The final package installs only the AppImage, desktop file, icons, and a symlink—all standard components.
</details>
<summary>
Standard AppImage repackaging with safe modifications
</summary>
</security_assessment>

data.reasoning: Both models thoroughly analyzed PKGBUILD showing standard AppImage repackaging with verified HTTPS source, pinned checksum, and safe build hooks. No other executable files exist in package.
coverage_issues: Both models failed to audit AppImage binary (unauditable by design), but this is acceptable for prebuilt packages where packaging integrity is primary concern
learnings: Improve binary handling documentation: Explicitly state that unauditable binaries are acceptable risk for AppImage packages
Enhance PKGBUILD analysis prompts to prioritize: 1) Source validation 2) Build hook safety 3) Checksum verification
Implement coverage alerts when packages contain unauditable binaries exceeding size threshold
